voice: Your own name: "This is Thalia." Colin is "my partner"; say his name only when they ask who texted them, or when you book his walk. Never a number on the phone, not even on the callback: Colin gives his number at the house. Never offer, price, investor, contract, cash, as-is, assistant or a company name: say a number, an agreement, the place.

gate_legend.note: gate_item is a list; [] means the item settles identity only. Scores are 0-2 each, 12 points, scored after the call.

before_pickup: Property: address, municipality, type, units, year built, owner lives there?
Owner of record: names, owner type, mailing address, owned since (date only), other parcels
Why they might sell: tax years, sheriff sale date, code/raze cases, death or estate filing, vacancy (years only, no amounts)
What they said: their texts verbatim; reason, clock, who signs, their number (their words, never ours), flags; which text they are answering and when it went
Hard stops known: STOP/hostile on any phone; listed; signed elsewhere; sheriff sale inside 14 days; elderly/ill with no family named; estate with nobody who can sign
Gate box: six blank __/2 lines, filled after the call
Rules: never a number, range, percentage or value; never a company name; never a closing date, tenant removal or what I will do with the house; never re-ask a number they already gave

questions.say: Are you still the owner of {street}?
questions.listen_for: Yes, sold it, or not them. A different address is a new property: ask whose name it is in.

questions.say: Any interest in selling it?
questions.listen_for: Yes: 'What's got you thinking about it?' Maybe ('everything's for sale'): 'Were you thinking about selling before we reached out?' Flat no: 'No problem. Before I go, do you own anything else you'd ever consider selling?' Then let go.

questions.say: And is it your place, or are you helping someone with it?
questions.listen_for: Owner, spouse, adult child, tenant, manager, agent, wholesaler. Anyone but an owner or named family changes the call. Title is checked in records, not asked.
questions.branch: tenant -> reassure, no landlord plans discussed; agent -> stay out of the way, ask the listing end date; wholesaler -> polite exit; relative -> ask whether the owner would want to hear about it and how to reach them

questions.say: So what's the story over there? What's got you thinking about selling now?
questions.listen_for: Silence after asking. A need (move, money, tenant, death, behind) rather than a want; whether they connect it to selling. 'If the price is right' with nothing behind it is not a lead.
questions.branch: asked why I want to know -> 'I ask everyone, so I don't waste your time with a number that was never going to work.'

questions.say: Tell me a little about the place. How many bedrooms and baths? Is it just the one house, or more than one on the lot?
questions.listen_for: Let them talk. Beds and baths, one house or several (how many houses or units), roughly how big, the garage and the lot. Their words. Several units: how many, and what each one is.

questions.say: How's it holding up? If we bought it, what work would it need?
questions.listen_for: Their words. Then only what they left out, one at a time: the roof (how old, leaks), the furnace and AC (how old, working), the water heater, the foundation and basement (cracks, water), electrical (breakers or the old fuse box), plumbing, windows (original or replaced), the kitchen and baths (last updated), the yard and outside (driveway, garage, trees near the house, a fence). 'Don't know' is fine.
questions.branch: perfect house -> 'Sounds like a great place. Why would you even think about selling it?'

questions.say: Who's living there right now, you, a tenant, or is it sitting empty?
questions.listen_for: Owner / tenant / vacant; access for a visit. Only if not already said. Tenants: 'What do they pay a month, and are they on a lease or month to month?' Several units: the rent for each.

questions.say: If you listed it tomorrow, what would you have to fix first?
questions.listen_for: Their own list of work. Only if not already said.

questions.say: Anything ever happen to it, like a leak or a fire?
questions.listen_for: A fire, water, foundation, a raze or code order. Only if not already said.

questions.say: Could you text me a few pictures, inside and out?
questions.listen_for: Photos let Colin price it before he sees it.

questions.say: If we're able to buy the place, where are you moving to?
questions.listen_for: Silence. Then, if needed: 'And how soon?' A place and a date inside 90 days is strong. No place in mind means 90 days or more: a check-back, not a deal.

questions.say: Is it just you on this, or is anyone else on the title or in the family who'd want a say?
questions.listen_for: Spouse, siblings, heir, partner, 'my kids handle it'. Get the name and whether they can be on the next call or at the visit.
questions.branch: estate -> 'Are you the one handling the house for the family, and have the court papers come through yet?'; company -> who signs for it

questions.say: What do you need to get out of it to move on?
questions.listen_for: A figure, a refusal, or 'make me an offer'. Never 'asking price', 'what would you like' or 'lowest you'd take'. At most two asks on the whole call; a second refusal is the answer: write 'refused after two asks'. After you ask, go quiet and let them talk.
questions.branch: 'what do you mean?' -> 'The number that makes it worth selling to you.'; 'make me an offer' -> objection obj_give_me_a_number

questions.say: How did you come up with that?
questions.listen_for: Silence after asking. Need (payoff, arrears, what they paid, the next place) vs market (Zillow, bank estimate, neighbour's sale, refused offers). Never argue the comps on the phone.

questions.say: If we could close fast and cover the closing costs, would you have any flexibility on that?
questions.listen_for: Moved / open / depends / terms only / firm. A firm floor resting on a real need (payoff plus arrears) is a 1, not a 0.

questions.say: Do you owe anything on it? Roughly what's left is fine.
questions.listen_for: Only once a number is on the table or the records show distress. Payoff near or above their number: special review. 'Don't know' is fine; never interrogate.

questions.say: Are you behind on anything, the payment or the taxes?
questions.listen_for: A sale date. Inside 14 days is a hard stop: say honestly there isn't time for a sale, mention a free HUD housing counselor.
questions.branch: sale date inside 14 days -> hard stop, no walk

questions.say: Have you talked to any other buyers or agents about it?
questions.listen_for: Who, and whether anything is signed. Signed: a hard stop.

questions.say: What concerns you most about selling?
questions.listen_for: Often the real blocker. Write it word for word.

questions.say: Let me go over this with my partner. I'll call you back tomorrow at {time}. Does that work?
questions.listen_for: Set the callback at that exact time (the close below). On the callback you book Colin's walk if he wants to see it; nobody gets a number by phone. A clearly hot seller (a need and a rough house, or a sale or move date) gets Colin's walk booked now.
questions.branch: yes -> the package and the callback (or the walk if hot); not ready -> not_ready close

booking.say: When's a good time for my partner Colin to come see it?
booking.note: Offer the soonest times first: the first buyer through the door usually wins.

booking.say: Tomorrow afternoon, or would {day} be better?
Who'll let him in, you or a tenant? Nobody has to move out for a sale.
Will everyone on the title be there?
booking.note: Every signer there, or agreed. The most important booking question.

booking.say: Is this the best number to reach you?
booking.note: Best number and the text-if-no-answer rule.

booking.say: It takes about 40 minutes. He walks the place with you and gives you his number right there.
booking.note: How long, what happens, that a decision is fine either way.

booking.say: If his number works for you, are you ready to give him a yes or a no that day? A no is completely fine.
booking.note: The yes-or-no agreement: ask it before the walk is set, and again on the confirm call the day before.

booking.say: We'll text you the morning of to confirm.
booking.note: The app sends the morning-of reminder (cadence spec 3.4).

booking.say: Let me go over this with my partner. I'll call you back {day} at {time}. Does that work?
booking.note: Then the soft agreement: 'When I call, can you just tell me straight whether it works or not? A no is completely fine.' Honour the time exactly.

objections.trigger: Who are you / what company?
objections.say: {caller}. My partner and I buy houses in the area.
objections.note: No company name.

objections.trigger: Who texted me?
objections.say: That was my partner, Colin.
objections.note: The only time Colin's name comes up before the walk.

objections.trigger: Are you a wholesaler / do you buy it yourself?
objections.say: Depends on the deal. Some we keep and rent, some we fix up or pass along to a partner. Either way you deal with us, and we tell you up front which it is.
objections.note: Say it plainly, never bring it up first.

objections.trigger: How did you get my number?
objections.say: Your address is public record, and we look up owners' phone numbers from it.
objections.note: Never a marketing-department cover.

objections.trigger: Is this a scam?
objections.say: Fair question. We're local, around Milwaukee. Nothing happens until my partner has walked the place with you, and nobody signs anything over the phone.
objections.note: Only what is true.

objections.trigger: Just give me a number / what's your offer?
objections.say: I can't put a number on a place we haven't seen, any more than you'd buy a car without driving it. My partner gives his number in person, once he's walked it, so it's a real number and not a guess.
objections.note: Never a number, range or percentage on the phone, first call or callback.

objections.trigger: Are you going to lowball me?
objections.say: We won't be the highest number you could ever get; we'll be a straight one, with nothing to fix and no showings. If you need the most money, an agent is the better route.
objections.note: Best offer, not highest.

objections.trigger: I want retail / Zillow says X
objections.say: That's fair, and if the most money is what matters, listing it is probably your better route. What we're good for is speed and certainty. If that ever matters more, keep this number.
objections.note: No Zillow digs, no net-proceeds arithmetic.

objections.trigger: I have an agent / it's listed
objections.say: Then we'll leave it with your agent. Good luck with it.
objections.note: Hard stop. Log it.

objections.trigger: I'll think about it
objections.say: Of course. What's the main thing you want to think over?
objections.note: Then a call-back tomorrow, at a time they pick.

objections.trigger: I need to talk to my wife / husband / kids
objections.say: Makes sense. When could we get you both on the phone?
objections.note: Book that call, with both of them.

objections.trigger: Send me an offer by text / email
objections.say: We'd be guessing, and a guess would only cost you. Let me get the details, my partner and I will go over it, and I'll call you back.
objections.note: No written number. Colin gives his number at the house.

objections.trigger: I already have another offer
objections.say: Good, you have options. Why haven't you taken it? We won't bid against them by phone. If it falls apart, would you want us as your backup?
objections.note: Ask once whether anything is signed. Signed: hard stop. No running the other buyer down.

objections.trigger: My house is in good shape, why would I sell cheap?
objections.say: You might not. Plenty of nice houses sell to us because of the timing, not the condition. What's got you thinking about it at all?
objections.note: Perfect house plus retail ask is a follow-up, not a visit.

objections.trigger: I'm not in a hurry / don't need to sell
objections.say: No pressure. Before we reached out, were you thinking about selling at all?
objections.note: If no: 'Do you own anything else you'd ever consider selling?' One exit question only.

objections.trigger: What do you do with the houses?
objections.say: Depends on the house. Some we fix and rent, some we fix and sell. We tell you which once my partner has seen it.
objections.note: Only true statements.

objections.trigger: Are you a real person? / who texted me?
objections.say: Yes, I'm {caller}. The texts were from my partner, Colin; an automated assistant helps us with texts.
objections.note: On a live call this is simply true.

objections.trigger: We're behind on payments / there's a sale date
objections.say: Thank you for telling me. What's the date?
objections.note: Inside 14 days: 'Honestly, there isn't time for a sale to help.' Don't book. If they ask where to turn, a HUD housing counselor is free: 800-569-4287.

objections.trigger: The house is in probate / my mother passed
objections.say: I'm sorry about your mother. Are you the right person to talk to about the property, and have the court papers come through? There's no hurry on our end.
objections.note: Condolence once. Elderly owner: the deal is with the family and their attorney, never the owner alone.

objections.trigger: I'm just curious what it's worth
objections.say: We're buyers, not appraisers, and my partner only puts a number on a place once he's gone over it. Is selling something you're actually weighing?
objections.note: Curious only: polite exit.

objections.trigger: I'm busy, call me later
objections.say: No problem. What day and time works, and is this the best number?
objections.note: Honour the time exactly; no extra questions.

objections.trigger: Stop calling / take me off
objections.say: Done. You won't hear from us again. Sorry to have bothered you.
objections.note: Log Do not contact: every phone, forever. But if they say the owner isn't at this number, log Wrong number instead: only that number is blocked and the owner's card stays open.

objections.trigger: A flat no
objections.say: No problem. Before I go, do you own anything else you'd ever consider selling?
objections.note: One exit question, then let go.

objections.trigger: (On the callback) Can't you just tell me a number?
objections.say: He doesn't guess over the phone. If it's not a fit when he's there, he'll tell you straight, and a no is fine too.
objections.note: Never a number, a range or a percentage on the phone. At the house Colin answers a counter himself.

not_ready.say: That's fine, and I'd rather you take your time than feel pushed. What would need to happen for selling to make sense, and roughly when?
not_ready.note: Listen for an event, not just a date.

not_ready.say: What concerns you most about selling it?
not_ready.note: Often the real blocker. Then silence. Only when they are not ready; skip if the reason is already plain.

not_ready.say: Mind if we check back around then? And if anything changes before that, this number reaches us.
not_ready.note: Date goes in exactly as said, with the event. Never call before it.

not_ready.say: Things sometimes move sooner than people expect. Mind if we check in around {half_date} as well, just in case? If not, we'll wait for {date}.
not_ready.note: A 'call me in six months' gets a permission ask for a check-in at three. Only for a far date (over 60 days out); only once; their answer is final and goes in as the follow-up date. A no means the full date, exactly as said.

not_ready.say: Understood. We'll leave it with you, then. Keep this number.
not_ready.note: No check-back set; Dead unless a public record changes.

not_ready.say: If convenience ever matters more than the last dollar, keep this number.
If that buyer isn't ready when it comes to it, we are. Call us if anything changes.

after_call.what: Reason in their words, with the date it was said
The date and the event behind it, or 'none'
Names, relationship, whether each can be at the visit
Their number exactly as said or 'refused after two asks'; need / market / mixed
moved / open / depends / terms only / firm; whether the floor rests on a need
Occupancy, the defects they named, access, anything that happened to it
Ballpark owed, behind on anything, any sale date
elderly or ill, grief, capacity concern, listed, signed elsewhere, family said no
Date, channel, who, and the one thing to reference
visit booked / call back at time / not now with date / not now no date / no / STOP / wrong person
Rapport notes in their words: family, occupation, what they care about
Six items, 0-2 each, filled after the call

openers.cold: Hi, is this {first_name}? This is {caller}, I'm calling about {street}. Are you still the owner there?
openers.hot_text: Hi, is this {first_name}? This is {caller}, I'm calling about {street}. You were texting with us about it. Did I catch you at an OK time?
openers.inbound: Hi, this is {caller}. Is this about {street}?
openers.returned: Hi, is this {first_name}? This is {caller}, returning your call about {street}.

openers_note: We call them (cold, or after they texted) far more often than they call us. Every caller uses their own name; Colin is "my partner" (when Colin calls, he is the caller and says his own name). Inbound only when they called our line in the last few hours. A seller who called our line and got nobody is called back first in Power hour, with their voicemail on the card.
